name: Achik-Tash Base Camp
near: Sary-Mogol (about 3000–3200 m; CBT gives 3200 m) — ~25 km to Tulpar-Kol and the camps (Visit Alay); also the village of Kashka-Suu, from which people ride horses to Tulpar-Kol (too.kg).
elev: About 3600 m (ak-sai.com, Central Asia Travel, Nomad's Land; ~12,000 feet per Univ. of Washington). The advanced camp / Camp 1 “Solnechny” (Sunny) — about 4200–4400 m (Central Asia Travel, Nomad's Land). Visit Alay mistakenly writes “Base Camp 4400 m”, nomadasaurus — “about 4000 m”.
short: Achik-Tash is the main base camp on the north side of Lenin Peak (7134 m) in the Trans-Alay Range, at an elevation of about 3600 m: yurt and tent camps of mountaineering companies, the starting point for ascents and treks.
desc: Achik-Tash is a valley and meadow at the foot of Lenin Peak (7134 m), where every summer (June — September) several mountaineering companies (Ak-Sai Travel, Central Asia Travel and others) and local yurt camps set up base camps. From here ascents of Lenin Peak start, via Camp 1 (~4400 m) and Travellers' Pass (~4150 m), as well as acclimatization outings to Yukhin Peak and Petrovsky Peak, and day walks to Lake Tulpar-Kol (~3500 m), ~4 km away. The camp lies about 25 km south of the village of Sary-Mogol in the Alay Valley; from Osh it is about 280 km and 5 hours by car along the Pamir Highway M41 via Taldyk Pass and Sary-Tash (Central Asia Travel). A border permit is needed to visit the area (tour.too.kg, Visit Alay, Central Asia Travel).
guide: Achik-Tash is a rare chance to see a seven-thousander almost from the door of your yurt: Lenin Peak rises above a green meadow at 3600 m, where edelweiss blooms in July. Even if you are not a mountaineer, come for 1–2 nights: a walk to the reddish shores of Tulpar-Kol (~4 km) and a hike toward Travellers' Pass give views of the glaciers without technical skills. The camps operate from late June to late August — at that time in the dining tent you can meet expeditions from all over the world. Arrange the border permit in advance (7–20 days), and after Osh give your body a night of acclimatization in Sary-Mogol. If you are lucky with the dates, in July Sary-Mogol hosts a festival of national games with yaks and horses (CBT).
see: The north face and glaciers of Lenin Peak (7134 m); the base camp meadow with edelweiss; Lake Tulpar-Kol with red slopes (~3500 m, ~4 km); the climb to Travellers' Pass (~4150 m); the acclimatization peaks Yukhin (5130 m) and Petrovsky; expedition infrastructure (dining tent, banya, gear shop).
skip: You are not ready to arrange a border permit in advance and pay for a transfer on a dirt road. You tolerate 3600 m and cold nights poorly (even in summer about zero). Views of Lenin Peak from Sary-Mogol or from Tulpar-Kol are enough for you.
diff: Access to the camp is not difficult: a car to the place, then short walks. A day walk to Tulpar-Kol is easy; the walk from Sary-Mogol is 8–9 h (Visit Alay); the hike to Camp 1 is moderate/hard, 4–6 h, and acclimatization is needed (Univ. of Washington; nomadasaurus 2026). Climbing Lenin Peak is a technical high-altitude expedition.
when: Late June — late August: Central Asia Travel camps operate ~28 June — 30 August, transfers 25 June — 1 September; the Ak-Sai camp — June — September. In July — the festival of games with yaks and horses in Sary-Mogol (the third weekend of July, Visit Alay). Out of season there is no infrastructure.
hours: Seasonal: the yurt/tent camps are open approximately from late June to late August — early September (ak-sai.com, centralasia-travel.com). Around the clock within the season; the limitation is the border regime.
daytime: Early morning — the clearest weather and a clean view of the summit; by midday clouds often gather over the peak (editorial). For the walk to Tulpar-Kol/Travellers' Pass, set out in the morning.
how: Osh → Gulcha → Taldyk Pass → Sary-Tash → west along the Alay Valley to Sary-Mogol (M41/the road to Daroot-Korgon) → south across the Kyzyl-Suu River on a dirt road ~25 km to Tulpar-Kol and Achik-Tash. From Osh about 280 km, ~5 h by car (Central Asia Travel). From Sary-Mogol: ~45 min by car, 4–5 h on horseback, 8–9 h on foot (Visit Alay).
needcar: Yes. There is no public transport to the camp: a marshrutka (minibus)/shared taxi to Sary-Mogol, then a taxi/4×4 / SUV from CBT (or a transfer by a mountaineering company), a horse or a walk.
self: Partly: experienced travelers get there on their own (a marshrutka (minibus) + a taxi in Sary-Mogol) and overnight in the camps or a tent. Formally a border permit for the Lenin Peak zone is required — arranged in advance through a travel agency/CBT (tour.too.kg, Visit Alay). Nomadasaurus (2026) writes that in practice the permit was not checked for Tulpar-Kol and the base camp — do not rely on that.
roadtype: To Sary-Mogol — paved M41 via Taldyk and Sary-Tash; from Sary-Mogol ~25 km of dirt road with a ford/bridge over the Kyzyl-Suu to Tulpar-Kol and the camps (Visit Alay: “45 minutes by car”); there are signposts to the camps. The condition after rain is not confirmed.
traveltime: From Osh — about 5 h by car (~280 km, Central Asia Travel); by public transport to Sary-Mogol 4–5 h + 45 min by taxi (nomadasaurus 2026; Visit Alay).
stay:
• Ak-Sai Travel, the Achik-Tash camp (3600 m, June — September): a yurt for two $65 (breakfast) / $75 (breakfast+dinner) / $85 (three meals); a tent for two $40/50/65; single supplement $30–35; 15 yurts, 10 glamping capsules, 54 tents (ak-sai.com, 2026).
• Central Asia Travel — the “Edelweiss Meadow” base camp with heated yurts, a sauna, Wi-Fi (prices per the price list, 2027 season: 28.06–30.08).
• Yurt camps at Tulpar-Kol (CBT and private): from 1000 som/night with breakfast and dinner (Visit Alay); ~$10 with meals per nomadasaurus 2026; a tent in designated places is free.
• Sary-Mogol guesthouses $15–20 (nomadasaurus, 2026).
net: Ak-Sai claims Wi-Fi (Starlink) and a mobile signal in the camp (ak-sai.com, 2026); Central Asia Travel — Wi-Fi in the base camp and Camp 1. Sary-Mogol has mobile 4G (nomadasaurus, 2026). Coverage of specific operators in the camp itself is not confirmed.
entry: There is no separate entry fee; a border permit is needed: 3000 som/person via tour.too.kg (covers all zones, 7 working days, apply 14 days ahead; 2026). Processing through CBT/Visit Alay takes 10–20 days (Visit Alay); nomadasaurus (2026) gives $65 and 5 days via CBT Sary-Mogol — the source probably mixes up the permit and the mountaineering permit. Climbing Lenin Peak requires separate permits through a mountaineering company.
transfer: Sary-Mogol → camp: from 1500 som per car (Visit Alay) / $10–15 (nomadasaurus 2026). Osh → Sary-Mogol: 300 som marshrutka (minibus) / 400 som shared taxi (nomadasaurus 2026). A direct Osh — Achik-Tash transfer from the mountaineering companies — per price list, exact 2026 prices not found.
bring: A passport and a printout of the border permit; warm clothes (about zero at night even in July), a down jacket, a hat and gloves; sunglasses and high-SPF cream; trekking boots; cash in som (no ATMs — editorial); a headlamp; a kit against altitude sickness (editorial).
warn: Border zone: without a permit you may have problems at checkpoints — arrange it 2–3 weeks ahead (tour.too.kg; Visit Alay). At 3600 m: risk of altitude sickness, don't go up from Osh in a single day without a night at an intermediate altitude (editorial). Above the camp — glaciers and crevasses, going to Camp 1 and higher only with experience/a guide. The weather changes quickly, and snow is possible in summer.
food: Meals at the camps — buffet/three meals a day (Ak-Sai) and home cooking at the Tulpar-Kol yurt camps (breakfast and dinner included in the price). From local herders you can try kymyz (fermented mare's milk) and ayran (editorial, general Alay practice; specific places not confirmed).
reviews: Google Maps: the camp's listing is not unambiguously matched (catalog check — “Ambiguous result”). Hotel aggregators (Hotels.com, Travelocity) have a listing “Achik Tash Base Camp Ak Sai Travel” — rating not checked. From travel notes: pros — views of Lenin Peak, the organization of the camps, Wi-Fi; cons — cold nights, altitude, prices higher than the local yurt camps (Visit Alay).
p.sum: The simplest way to get there: Osh → Sary-Mogol (marshrutka (minibus) 300 som at 14:00 or a transfer), a night of acclimatization in Sary-Mogol, then a taxi along the dirt road ~25 km (1500 som per car) to Tulpar-Kol and the camps. Arrange the border permit (3000 som via tour.too.kg) 2–3 weeks ahead. Overnight in yurt camps at Tulpar-Kol (from ~1000 som with meals) or in the mountaineering companies' camps on the Achik-Tash meadow (Ak-Sai $65–85 for a yurt for two). The best day outings are to Travellers' Pass (4130 m) and Yukhin Peak (5130 m) after acclimatization.

p.iti.1.title: 3 days from Osh
p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: Osh → Sary-Mogol (marshrutka (minibus) 14:00), a night in a guesthouse. Day 2: a taxi to Tulpar-Kol, a walk to BC, a night in a yurt. Day 3: sunrise at the lake, Travellers' Pass, return to Sary-Mogol/Osh.
p.iti.2.title: Combinations
p.iti.2.plan: Along one road: Taldyk → Sary-Tash → Sary-Mogol → Tulpar-Kol → Achik-Tash. By trek — from Kojokelen over Jiptyk (3 days).
p.season: June: the camps open ~25–28.06, snow on the passes. July — August: peak season, expeditions, the games festival in Sary-Mogol (the third weekend of July), about 0 °C at night. September: the companies wrap up ~30.08–1.09, some private yurts operate until late September. October — May: no infrastructure, snow.
p.budget.economy: Marshrutka (minibus) Osh — Sary-Mogol 300 som + a taxi to the lake 1500 som/car (~400–750 per person) + a yurt at Tulpar-Kol ~1000–2000 som with meals + the border permit 3000 som ≈ 5000–6000 som/person for 2 days
p.budget.comfort: A transfer Osh — BC $300 per car + an Ak-Sai yurt $75–85 (for two with meals) + a horse $15/h + a sauna $25 ≈ $250–350/person for 2–3 days
p.permits: A border permit for the Lenin Peak zone is mandatory: via tour.too.kg — 3000 som, 5–7 working days (office at Isanov St. 105/3, Bishkek); via CBT/a tour operator — 10–20 days, $40–65 (travelers' logs). Apply 2–3 weeks ahead, and keep the printout and your passport with you. Climbing Lenin Peak requires a separate mountaineering permit through a company.
p.access: Children with mountain experience and adults without chronic illnesses — yes, but 3600 m requires acclimatization (a night in Sary-Mogol). Older people — only with caution and short walks. Stroller — no (dirt, tall grass). Dogs — at Ak-Sai a $20/day surcharge.
